```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Problem 1

```{r load-penguins}
data("penguins", package = "palmerpenguins")
```

The penguins dataset has `r nrow(penguins)` rows and `r ncol(penguins)` columns. It contains data on penguins near Palmer Station in Antarctica.

The species are `r paste(levels(penguins$species), collapse = ", ")`. The islands are `r paste(levels(penguins$island), collapse = ", ")`. Other variables include bill_length_mm, bill_depth_mm, flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g, sex, and year. Bill and flipper measurements are in millimeters. Body mass is in grams. Sex includes female and male, with some missing values. The years range from `r min(penguins$year)` to `r max(penguins$year)`.

The mean flipper length is `r round(mean(penguins$flipper_length_mm, na.rm = TRUE), 2)` mm. Missing values are left out.

```{r penguin-plot}
penguin_plot = ggplot(
  penguins,
  aes(
    x = bill_length_mm,
    y = flipper_length_mm,
    color = species
  )
) +
  geom_point(na.rm = TRUE) +
  labs(
    x = "Bill length (mm)",
    y = "Flipper length (mm)",
    color = "Species"
  )

penguin_plot

ggsave(
  filename = "penguin_scatterplot.png",
  plot = penguin_plot,
  width = 7,
  height = 5,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 300
)
```

## Problem 2

```{r create-data}
set.seed(123)

variable_types = tibble(
  normal_sample = rnorm(10),
  is_positive = normal_sample > 0,
  letter = letters[1:10],
  group = factor(
    rep(c("A", "B", "C"), length.out = 10),
    levels = c("A", "B", "C")
  )
)

variable_types
```

```{r calculate-means}
mean(pull(variable_types, normal_sample))
mean(pull(variable_types, is_positive))
mean(pull(variable_types, letter))
mean(pull(variable_types, group))
```

The mean works for normal_sample and is_positive. For is_positive, TRUE counts as 1 and FALSE counts as 0. Its mean is the share of sample values greater than zero.

The means of letter and group return NA with warnings. mean() does not treat text or factors as numbers.

```{r convert-types, echo = TRUE, results = "hide", warning = FALSE}
as.numeric(pull(variable_types, is_positive))
as.numeric(pull(variable_types, letter))
as.numeric(pull(variable_types, group))
```

TRUE becomes 1 and FALSE becomes 0, so their mean works. The letters become NA with a warning because they cannot be read as numbers. The factor becomes 1, 2, and 3 for A, B, and C. These numbers only label groups, so their average is not useful. R does not use these numbers when taking the mean of a factor without converting it first.
